Low relative humidity (often below 30%) and the urban heat island effect amplify radiative warming, pushing the thermometer higher than the August climatological average of ~23–25°C.

A broader regional heat wave and above-normal temperatures across central and southeastern Brazil have reinforced trader consensus around these values, while the absence of precipitation or cold-front influence until later in the week reduces downside risk. The market’s heavy weighting on 32°C (62%) versus 31°C (32%) reflects slight model or observational variance in exact peak timing and measurement site, with negligible probabilities assigned to extremes outside this narrow band. New observational data from afternoon readings or updated model runs could still shift resolution within the final hours.
